survivingClaim: Nothing about zeros of zeta. For the rank-one Levi: the Maass-Selberg inequality (I) for all T>=1 is equivalent to N(omega)=z(1-S)/(1+S), S=e^(-xz)M(z), being a Nevanlinna function of omega=z^2 (proved; classical in content), and this property is preserved under multiplication of M by Blaschke factors over non-real conjugate pairs (or real double zeros) anywhere in Re z>0 and by locally uniform limits (proved). Hence T-NR (c>2, b<1/2) and the control BLS satisfy S2-S4 with zeros off Re z=1/2, and (I) alone gives no constraint on numerator zeros. Relative to the recalled loop-group normalisation (sources not opened): affine SL_2 constant-term coefficients are chain products of M at z+kc, kc-z; in the chamber 0<Re z<Re c every denominator argument has Re>1; at c=1 every non-identity coefficient equals xi(z)/xi(z+n). DH shows no failure of the formal inequality at computed heights and has no zero with Re s>1 below height 2000 (measured for Re<=1.5, bound for Re>=1.5). Formal E_a fails on grids (measured). Closure for the two-variable affine kernel is argued, not proved. Verdict precise-obstruction stands with scope "rank-one proved, affine argued".

lesson: Positivity of truncated Eisenstein norms and Langlands-Shahidi non-vanishing act on denominators xi(u+1), which stay at Re >= 1 wherever the mechanism applies; strip arguments are zeros of scattering coefficients, and the inequality is closed under inner (Blaschke) factors. The affine Weyl shift moves the chamber, not the information. Pre-filter for any scattering carrier: does the inequality survive multiplying the coefficient by a Blaschke product over non-real conjugate pairs? T-NR with c>2 is such a product.
